limitations: Synthetic local datasets and instrumented service-owner reads, not production latency or live acceptance.
Reduced fixture schema with selected real migrations/indexes; each full report contains exact installed table/index catalog.
Unresolved: estimated unallocated freight and no lot lineage. Posted: real receipts, cost applications and untransformed unsold lots; supplier estimates remain provisional.
No broad sales-history/forecast-volume or transformed-lot stress profile; three serial samples per owner share OS/PostgreSQL caches.

The local PostgreSQL cluster has shared_buffers=400kB and work_mem=4MB. Initial posted-100 timings increased despite fewer queries; a subsequent quiet baseline/current pair had lower medians for four health/list owners and a slightly higher PO-summary median. Order, cache and scheduling effects are not isolated, and neither experiment establishes a blanket latency guarantee or production SLO.
Process RSS includes retained diagnostic results and is not an allocation profile.
Per-shipment supplier-cost review and accepted/reconciled freshness reads remain, preserving their original safety bounds; cost health still scales with eligible shipments.

limitations: Synthetic local posted shipments with five lines each and one PO linked to 100 shipments; no production statistics or records.
Original PostgreSQL 17.11 settings are preserved, including shared_buffers=400kB. The baseline runs before current; execution-order, cache and scheduling effects are not isolated.
Each run uses a fresh database, actual receipt closing and cost revision application, then read-only measurements. Caches and host scheduling are not experimentally controlled.
Per-shipment supplier review remains; the unchanged supplier query fingerprints, call counts and row volumes identify repeat work without proving a specific production SLO or CPU cause.
